name: Trotter Q9 quadruped
description: A ~9 kg research quadruped in the MIT Mini Cheetah mould: 12 quasi-direct-drive actuators (8318-class BLDC + 6:1 planetary), belt-driven knees with the knee motor carried high on the thigh, 6S LiPo, Raspberry Pi 5 + Teensy real-time controller. Hand-written test fixture and demo design.

wiring.name: CAN FD bus, front drivers (daisy chain)
CAN FD bus, rear drivers (daisy chain)
USB 3, Raspberry Pi to depth camera

behavior.description: Trotting gait: diagonal leg pairs in phase, 2 Hz, 12 cm stride (~0.4 m/s).

assumptions: Belt pre-tension maintained by an eccentric idler (not modelled).
Driver boards share the battery bus directly; regen absorbed by the LiPo.
Carbon tube strength is a conservative first-ply-failure allowable.

All 12 moteus controllers share one 5 Mbit/s CAN FD bus from the Teensy's CAN3 port through the transceiver (termination switched on at the transceiver and the last driver). Split onto a second bus if a higher control rate is needed.
The e-stop latches the power distribution board's switch input, which cuts every driver output; the logic rail is fed from the same board, so the computers also shut down.
Not modelled: battery strap and tray, board standoffs and screws, connectors and crimps, and a vent for the drivers' heat. The battery charger is off-board.
